paper_title: First results from BRASS-p broadband searches for hidden photon dark matter
notes: BRASS-p achieved record sensitivity of (0.3–1.0)×10^-13 to kinetic mixing chi in the mass range 49.63–74.44 μeV (12–18 GHz). The paper reports measurements from first science run (SR1) consisting of SR1a (12–16 GHz) and SR1b (14–18 GHz) with total measurement times of ~126 hours combined. The sensitivity varies across the frequency range; Figure 11 shows chi ≲ 10^-13 over the full range. The lower bound (3.0e-14) represents the best sensitivity achieved at higher frequencies (around 18 GHz / 74.44 μeV), while 1.0e-13 represents the sensitivity at lower frequencies (around 12 GHz / 49.63 μeV). The experiment assumes unpolarized hidden photon dark matter with local DM density ρ_DM = 0.3 GeV/cm³ (standard halo model). No signal candidates were found; limits are derived from cumulative noise spectra reaching σ_det ≈ 10^-23 W.
